evidence: Cic. Att. 1.14: aliēnārī ā senātū (Lewis & Short s.v. aliēnō)
terms.comment: “Become estranged from someone” is the passive, aliēnārī ab aliquō; the participle aliēnātus is the commonest form of the verb (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: estrange someone from oneself, alienate someone
evidence: Caes. BG 7.10: omnium suōrum voluntātēs aliēnāre (Lewis & Short: “sc. ā sē”)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short s.v. aliēnō: “to alienate, estrange, set at variance”.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 310.
